questions.q: Why did the Solara ML Platform team split the single `training` namespace into `training-lm` and `training-mm`?
options: To run two separate Kubernetes clusters
So the language-modeling and multimodal teams' jobs could be monitored and, later, cost-attributed separately on the same shared cluster
Because Kubernetes requires one namespace per node
To double the cluster's total GPU count
questions.explain: Both teams still share the solara-train cluster; separate namespaces make it possible to break monitoring and cost data down per team instead of only seeing a cluster-wide total.

questions.q: What does NVIDIA DCGM Exporter do?
options: It schedules GPU workloads onto nodes
It exposes GPU hardware counters, read by DCGM, as a Prometheus metrics endpoint
It compiles CUDA kernels for faster execution
It manages Kubernetes RBAC for GPU access
questions.explain: DCGM reads hardware counters directly off each GPU; DCGM Exporter exposes those counters in a format Prometheus can scrape like any other target.

questions.q: What does the `DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL` metric actually measure?
options: The percentage of the GPU's theoretical FLOPs being used
The percentage of time at least one kernel was executing on the GPU
The GPU's current temperature in Celsius
The number of training steps completed per second
questions.explain: GPU_UTIL reports whether something was running on the GPU's streaming multiprocessors — occupancy, not how efficiently that time was spent computing.

questions.q: A GPU shows high `DCGM_FI_DEV_GPU_UTIL` but low `DCGM_FI_PROF_PIPE_TENSOR_ACTIVE`. What does this combination suggest?
options: The GPU is defective and should be replaced
Training is running at maximum efficiency
The GPU looks busy, but something upstream — like data loading or communication — is leaving real compute capacity unused
The checkpoint has become corrupted
questions.explain: High occupancy with low tensor-core activity means the GPU is doing something, but not much useful math — a specific, actionable sign of an upstream bottleneck.

questions.q: What does `DCGM_FI_DEV_FB_USED` track, and why does it matter?
options: Network bandwidth used by a pod, to catch NCCL communication issues
GPU frame buffer (memory) usage, useful for catching memory creeping toward an out-of-memory failure
The number of failed training steps
Disk I/O throughput on the node's local NVMe
questions.explain: FB_USED reports GPU memory consumption; tracking it across a job's pods helps catch a memory leak or growth trend before it crashes the job.
